title: [Bug]: querynode crash when running cluster in k8
body: I installed Milvus 2.4.6 in cluster mode on Ubuntu with MicroK8s using the default Helm chart values, Kafka, and MinIO storage. The QueryNode always enters an error state. Its logs say the remote chunk-manager precheck cannot list objects in milvus-bucket because the X-Amz-Credential date has an incorrect format and must use yyyyMMdd, followed by "QueryNode init segcore failed."

symptoms_visible: My QueryNode repeatedly crashes during startup.
The logs say ListObjects failed because the date in X-Amz-Credential has an incorrect format and then report "QueryNode init segcore failed."
N0.label: N0 QueryNode storage precheck crash reported

symptoms_visible: The QueryNode still crashes with the same X-Amz-Credential date-format error while using the MinIO configuration from the Helm deployment.
N1.label: N1 bundled MinIO and Helm changes established

symptoms_visible: After adding S3 permissions and switching to a standalone MinIO outside the Milvus Helm deployment, the QueryNode still reports the same X-Amz-Credential date-format error.
N2_x.label: N2_x permissions and standalone MinIO aftermath

symptoms_visible: The QueryNode continues to crash on the MinIO ListObjects precheck with the credential-date error, and I am not using IAM.
N3.label: N3 IAM ruled out

symptoms_visible: It works now; the QueryNode no longer fails startup with the MinIO credential-date error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after clock correction

question_patterns: Are you using an external S3 service or the MinIO deployed by the Milvus Helm chart?
How is the object storage deployed for this cluster?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I use MinIO as the S3 storage. At this point I am using the MinIO from the Milvus Helm installation, not an external MinIO.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am using AWS S3 with IAM authentication rather than MinIO.
It is the bundled MinIO under a different Helm release name.

question_patterns: Please share all changes you made to the Helm values.
Did you enable access control or customize the MinIO settings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I followed the milvus-helm chart 4.2.0. The only change I made was changing the Milvus image tag from 2.4.6 to v2.4.6-gpu and requesting GPUs for the QueryNode and IndexNode; the MinIO values use minioadmin, milvus-bucket, rootPath file, and useIAM false.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I enabled IAM and supplied custom credentials and an IAM endpoint in the Helm values.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's c4 and c7: msr120295 explains that the deployment initially uses the Helm-provided MinIO and posts the changed values. This edge describes only the opening reporter's MicroK8s cluster.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as an S3 authorization or MinIO deployment problem by adding storage permissions and moving to a separately deployed MinIO.
solution.concrete_example: Add the required S3 permissions and configure Milvus to use a standalone MinIO deployment, then restart the QueryNode.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's c3-c8: after the permission direction was raised, msr120295 added S3 permissions and used a standalone MinIO outside the Milvus Helm release, but reported the identical error. This persistent deployment change is S2 and the direction is falsified for this reporter.

question_patterns: Is IAM enabled for this MinIO configuration?
Are you using IAM authentication rather than the configured MinIO access and secret keys?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, I am not using IAM.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, useIAM is enabled and the workload obtains credentials through an IAM endpoint.
No, IAM is disabled, but my bucket has a different display name in the MinIO console.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's c9-c10: xiaofan-luan asks whether IAM is enabled and msr120295 explicitly says it is not. Later Docker Compose and bare-metal reports by other participants are separate deployments and are not merged into this causal chain.

solution.intent: Correct and synchronize the host and Kubernetes node clocks because the MinIO client generates the X-Amz-Credential automatically and a large system-clock offset is corrupting the signed S3 request date.
solution.concrete_example: Check the host and every MicroK8s node with date or timedatectl, enable NTP synchronization, correct any large offset, restart the affected Milvus pods, and verify that the QueryNode starts without the ListObjects credential-date error.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the malformed X-Amz-Credential date error, ruled out IAM, and showed that changing permissions and MinIO deployment did not alter it. The engineer concluded that the automatically generated signature date was wrong because the system clock had a large offset; the reporter subsequently confirmed that it worked.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's c19-c21: xiaofan-luan narrows the date-signature failure to the system clock, notes that X-Amz-Credential is generated automatically by the MinIO client, and asks the reporter to check for a huge offset. msr120295 then confirms, 'it works now.' The later 169.254.169.254 diagnosis concerns grebois's separate bare-metal deployment and is deliberately not spliced into the opening reporter's resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the opening reporter's resolved cause as a large system-clock offset affecting the automatically generated S3/MinIO X-Amz-Credential date.
Must ground the diagnosis in the credential date-format error, the absence of IAM, and the unchanged failure after adding permissions and moving to standalone MinIO.
Must recommend correcting and synchronizing the host and MicroK8s node clocks, such as through NTP, before restarting the affected Milvus pods.
Must not present S3 permission changes, switching MinIO deployments, or changing Milvus versions as the fix; those directions did not remove this reporter's error.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the QueryNode starts without the ListObjects credential-date error before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Infrastructure user comfortable with Kubernetes, MicroK8s, Helm values, Kafka, MinIO, and GPU resource requests, but reliant on maintainers for diagnosing S3 signature behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, cooperative, and configuration-focused; posts logs and values when requested, asks for concrete working Helm settings, and confirms succinctly when the issue is resolved.
